instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it in a rice cooker or a covered pot.
In a small microwave-safe bowl, stir together 1/4 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup mirin, 1/4 cup sake and 2 tbsp sugar. Microwave it for 30 seconds and stir until the sugar has dissolved.

Lay the 2 lb chicken thighs smooth side down on a board. Cut shallow slits about 1/2 inch apart across the thick parts, without cutting all the way through, and press each thigh open with your fingers so it's an even thickness all over.
Pat the thighs dry with paper towels and sprinkle both sides with the 1/8 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Lay in half the thighs smooth side down and cook for 5 minutes without moving them, until the underside is deep golden and lets go of the pan.
Flip them, turn the heat down to low, cover the pan and cook for 3 minutes. Move them to a plate.
Turn the heat back up to medium-high, add the other 1 tbsp oil and cook the second batch the same way.
Put the first batch back in the pan. Wipe up the fat around the chicken with a folded paper towel held in tongs. The pan is hot.

Turn the heat to medium and pour in the sauce. Let it bubble for 3 to 4 minutes, turning the chicken and spooning the sauce over it, until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the chicken. You're cooking it to 175°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink left.

Move the chicken to a board and let it rest for 2 minutes. If the sauce in the pan is still thin, let it bubble for another minute. Take it off the heat while it's still a little runny. It thickens as it cools.
Thinly slice 2 of the green onions. Slice the chicken across into strips about 1 inch wide.
Taste the sauce, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Serve the chicken over the rice with the sauce spooned over and the green onions on top.
method_notes: All three cook the thighs in a skillet first and only then add a sauce of soy sauce, mirin, sugar and sake (or water) to reduce into a glaze around them. Just One Cookbook, the lead, scores the thighs to an even thickness, sears them smooth side down for 5 minutes, steams them covered on low for 3, wipes out the fat and glazes them in a 2:2:2:1 sauce of soy, mirin, sake and sugar. Viet World Kitchen reduces the sauce separately for 20 minutes and uses only a little to glaze, and Khin's Kitchen cooks skin-on thighs with ginger in the sauce and a crunchy slaw alongside. This one doubles the lead's sauce for 2 lb of thighs, cooks them in two batches and serves them over short-grain rice with green onions as Viet World Kitchen does.
